name: WebGL
summary: A browser graphics API that exposes an OpenGL ES-derived state machine through JavaScript contexts, typed resource objects, shader programs, and security-constrained framebuffer presentation.

features.name: Context-owned graphics state machine
features.description: A WebGLRenderingContext owns bindings, capabilities, programs, framebuffer state, and error state; commands mutate this context and subsequent commands observe the current bindings.
benefits: Maps a portable JavaScript API onto ordered graphics operations
costs: Implicit state and context loss make ordering and lifecycle correctness difficult

features.name: Typed GPU resource handles
features.description: WebGL exposes typed opaque objects such as buffers, textures, shaders, programs, and framebuffers; creation, binding, configuration, and deletion occur through the context API.
benefits: Separates resource identity from JavaScript object representation
costs: Applications must track bindings, compatibility, and deletion across asynchronous GPU work

features.name: Browser security and presentation boundary
features.description: WebGL integrates GPU rendering with a browser canvas and applies browser security, origin, context-creation, and context-loss rules around access to graphics resources and presented pixels.
benefits: Makes GPU rendering available without granting native process privileges
costs: Browser policy and context loss constrain portability and determinism

mathematical_views.model: Labeled transition system for context state
mathematical_views.question: Which graphics state results from an ordered sequence of WebGL commands, and which commands are valid in that state?
assumptions: The context state is the complete modeled state
Commands are ordered transitions with validation outcomes
GPU execution details are abstracted behind command effects

mathematical_views.question: How do shader, buffer, texture, program, and framebuffer handles connect to context bindings and draw operations?
assumptions: Opaque WebGL objects are resource nodes
The graph models API relationships rather than physical driver allocation

benefits: Compact API for ordered graphics commands
costs: Hidden bindings create state leakage and ordering bugs

benefits: Explicit resource categories and reusable handles
costs: Resource lifetime and binding compatibility remain application responsibilities

benefits: Native-like GPU access within browser isolation
costs: Context loss, policy, and implementation differences reduce guarantees
